clue.text: In another country, hiding Turkish title for rock album

indicators.note: something hiding another thing keeps it tucked inside, so one word wraps round the other

blocks.note: living in another country is living abroad
a bey was a governor or nobleman in the Ottoman Empire

explanation.surface: A rock album gets a Turkish title for its release overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: A bey was a provincial governor in the Ottoman Empire, the title placed after a name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles' 1969 LP, named after the London street where their studio stood, is a famous rock record.

clue.text: Rent: it stars singers and dancers

indicators.note: rent means torn apart, so the letters that follow are ripped up and put back in another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A note about the musical Rent: its cast is full of singing, dancing stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' reads as the title of the Broadway musical; here it is the past tense of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: Performers such as singers and dancers are called artists or artistes.

clue.text: Explosion of Internet writing about victory over gutless ref

indicators.note: something about another goes round it, so one word encloses the next
without guts means the middle has been removed

blocks.note: a blog is a web log
a win is a victory
an ump, short for umpire, is a referee

explanation.surface: An online row erupts after a win over a feeble referee.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the first part above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Blowing up is the act of detonating, so the gerund names an explosion.

clue.text: Flunky in health club mixed up names

indicators.note: things mixed up are confused, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: the Y is American shorthand for the YMCA, a gym and health club
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gym lackey gets the members' names muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: A yes-man is a servile follower who agrees with everything, much like a flunky.

clue.text: Attack Rolling Stone

indicators.note: something rolling tumbles over, so its letters turn up in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Rolling Stone, Mick or Keith perhaps, goes on the offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling Stone' looks like the band or the magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is an assault, as in the onset of an enemy, as well as the start of something.

clue.text: Made a call and did no prep, unfortunately

indicators.note: something gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters come out in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone phoned in to a meeting without having done their homework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made a call' suggests the telephone; here it means a visit.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop in is to pay someone a casual visit, an old sense of making a call.

clue.text: Vain reminder about university

indicators.note: one thing about another goes round it, so a word encloses a letter

blocks.note: a prod is a nudge to jog someone's memory
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A vain little memo about a college.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone vain thinks too well of themselves, which is the conceited sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Cachet of dissolute priest, e.g.

indicators.note: dissolute means loose-living, and loose letters can be put back together differently

blocks.note: e.g. supplies the letters EG

explanation.surface: The standing enjoyed by, say, a debauched clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Cachet is distinction or high status, the same sense as prestige.

clue.text: Mediterranean flora exist in stereo, strangely

indicators.note: something done strangely is out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged
one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: to live is to exist
taken as written

explanation.surface: Plants of southern Europe oddly playing on a sound system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' acts on stereo alone, and the result is split after its first letter to take the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive groves are typical vegetation around the Mediterranean, so the trees are plant life of that region.

clue.text: Shifts locations without a bit of publicity

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letters named are taken away

blocks.note: an address is where something is located
an ad, a single advertisement, is one piece of publicity

explanation.surface: A business moves premises without any press coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shifts' looks like a verb about moving; it is the plural noun for simple dresses.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a loose, straight frock, so shifts are a kind of women's garment.

clue.text: End of trumpet solo ruined instruments

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept
something ruined is wrecked and broken up, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the final letter of trumpet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trumpeter's solo ends badly, ruined along with the band's instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Tools are implements, and an instrument is a tool for doing a job.

clue.text: Herons lie all over the place!

definitions.text: Herons lie all over the place!

indicators.note: things all over the place are scattered, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Wading birds are everywhere you look.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: herons stand about all along the water's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Herons are wading birds that stalk the shallows, so the coastline is where you find them lying about.

clue.text: Turn a circuit, keeping time for the band whose amp goes up to here

definitions.text: the band whose amp goes up to here

indicators.note: a thing keeping something holds it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: to spin is to turn round
taken as written
a lap is one circuit of a track
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Do a lap of the track in time, says someone describing a band.
explanation.walkthrough: In the film This Is Spinal Tap the band's amplifiers go up to eleven, and this is 11 Across, so 'here' means eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinal Tap is the fictional heavy-metal group of the 1984 mockumentary, famous for amps whose dials reach eleven.

clue.text: See 7
Long story is fun if you read it backward

indicators.note: reading something from the end to the start turns its letters round

blocks.note: a gas is informal for great fun

explanation.surface: A tale that is only enjoyable if you start at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer from the right and it says A GAS, which is fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long, rambling narrative, originally a Norse tale of heroes.

clue.text: Extraordinary debts following expert at archeological site

indicators.note: one thing following another comes after it, so the debts are placed last, behind the expert and the site

blocks.note: a pro is an expert
an excavation is called a dig
IOUs are notes acknowledging debts

explanation.surface: An expert at an excavation runs up remarkable debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' places the debts after the expert at the site.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodigious means enormous or remarkable, so it is a synonym of extraordinary.

clue.text: Talk about fashionable top keeping the water out

indicators.note: one word about another wraps round it

blocks.note: to rap is to talk freely, in old slang
in means in fashion
a roof is the top of a building

explanation.surface: Chatter about a stylish hat that keeps off the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: Rap as a verb for chatting is older American slang, before the music took the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainproof describes material that resists water, so it keeps showers from soaking through.

clue.text: One enters to refill damaged part of an engine

indicators.note: one thing that enters others goes in among them
something damaged is broken up, so these letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mechanic goes in to top up a broken component of a motor.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil filter strains impurities from a car engine's lubricant, so it is a component of the motor.

clue.text: Demonstrations in support of taxes

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
to tax someone is to strain or test them

explanation.surface: Rallies held in favour of higher taxation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taxes' is a verb here: a hard task taxes or tests you.
explanation.definitionFit: Protests are public demonstrations of objection, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Insults one among like people…

indicators.note: one thing among others sits in their midst, so a letter goes inside a word

blocks.note: as means like, as in 'as good as new'
persons is a plural of person
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is insulted when singled out among a group of similar folk.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs the surface on into the next clue, but each clue is solved on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspersions are damaging remarks, as in casting aspersions, so they are insults.

clue.text: Fruit company invested in a whirlwind trip

indicators.note: a whirlwind spins things round, so these letters are tossed into a new order
money invested in something is put inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
Co. is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A produce firm puts money into a hasty journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whirlwind trip' reads as a rushed tour; whirlwind acts on trip alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a small orange stone fruit.

clue.text: …and promotes ousting leader of Germany

indicators.note: to oust is to throw out, so a letter is removed from the word
'leader of' keeps only the first letter of 'Germany'

blocks.note: to plug a product is to advertise it
the first letter of Germany

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: someone pushes a cause by getting rid of Germany's chancellor.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses join this clue to 18 Across in the surface only; the definition is just the opening 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plus is used as a conjunction meaning in addition, so it can replace 'and'.

clue.text: Detected a trap inside Michigan city

indicators.note: inside means within, so one piece is put in the middle of another

blocks.note: to see something is to detect it
taken as written
a gin is a snare or trap for game

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a snare set within a Michigan town.
explanation.walkthrough: A gin as a trap is an old sense, surviving in the term gin trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Saginaw is a city in the state of Michigan, on the river of the same name.

clue.text: Said "swallow" as a joke

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so the word is judged by how it is pronounced

blocks.note: to ingest is to swallow food

explanation.surface: Someone told to swallow something meant it only as a gag.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in jest is meant humorously, not seriously, so it is done for a laugh.

clue.text: Conservatives' celebration is broadcast

definitions.note: the right is a collective noun for conservatives, so a plural defines it

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard over the air, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a rite is a ceremonial celebration

explanation.surface: A party held by conservatives is put out on television.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's ties the definition to the wordplay: the conservatives' word is a sound-alike of the celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: The right is the political wing made up of conservatives, as opposed to the left.

clue.text: Painful sound from out-of-tune organ

indicators.note: an out-of-tune instrument is out of order, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The awful noise a badly tuned church instrument makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A groan is a low moan uttered in pain or distress.

clue.text: Members of group aren't (in general) taking care of children

indicators.note: members are parts of a larger body, so the answer is made of parts of the following words

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of group through to the start of general

explanation.surface: People in some club are not, as a rule, minding the kids.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets and apostrophe are ignored: groUP AREN'T IN General.
explanation.definitionFit: Parenting is the work of raising and looking after one's offspring.

clue.text: Mountain crest facing away from overpass

indicators.note: a word's facing is its front, and it going away means the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: a bridge carries a road over another

explanation.surface: A peak's summit looking away from a flyover.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is the long narrow top of a mountain range, its crest line.

clue.text: Sorcerer, half looking back at weapon: "You're wasting your time with this?"

definitions.text: You're wasting your time with this?

indicators.note: half a word keeps only one of its halves, the rest being dropped
looking back means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written; its first four letters are kept
a sword is a bladed weapon

explanation.surface: A wizard glances at a weapon and scoffs at the time being wasted.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a self-referential joke: the solver is wasting time on the very thing being clued.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle like this one is a pastime, the kind of thing a scold says you are frittering hours away on.

clue.text: Consumed and vanquished, having lost first place

indicators.note: losing the first position means the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: to be vanquished is to be beaten

explanation.surface: A team, eaten up and defeated, has lost its top ranking.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been consumed has been eaten, the past participle of eat.

clue.text: Head of CIA abandoning clothes in African capital

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter
to abandon something is to leave it behind, so a letter is taken out

blocks.note: tunics are loose garments
the opening letter of CIA

explanation.surface: The CIA's chief ditches his disguise in a North African city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis is the capital city of Tunisia, on the Mediterranean coast of North Africa.

clue.text: Worth undertaking after a foul?

blocks.note: surface reading: something worth doing because it costs nothing
setter's reading: in basketball, a shot awarded after an infringement, taken unopposed from the line

explanation.walkthrough: 'Worth undertaking' hints at a costless attempt; the foul makes it basketball.
explanation.definitionFit: In basketball a player who is fouled gets unopposed shots at the basket, each worth one point.
